paper_style.palette_strategy: 冷蓝架构框与 ours/highlight 行为主，紫橙绿蓝承担多模型曲线类别，Appendix 数据流程增加橙红标题、蓝数据库和绿色 check；照片 montage 使用自然色而非量化 palette。颜色语义清晰但跨对象没有公开 palette 常量，曲线和高亮行的灰度冗余不足。
paper_style.vector_raster_mix: 正文、表线、箭头和部分文字是 PDF vector/text；生成照片、Figure 1 patch thumbnails、Figure 2/4/A1/A4/A5 图像、Figure A3 histograms 和 Figure A2 raster elements 是 raster/JPX，整体为 mixed rendering。公开仓库未提供对应绘图源。
paper_style.style_consistency: 正文、caption、表格均保持 ICLR 单栏 Nimbus/Computer Modern 体系，表格横线和 ours 行高亮稳定；raster figure 内部引入 sans-serif/Calibri/Times，图内字号偏小，且颜色与形状冗余不一致。

figures.label: Figure 1

caption.text: Figure 1: Overview of NextStep-1 Framework. NextStep-1 employs a causal transformer to process tokenized text and image tokens. During training, Flow Matching Head predicts the continuous flow from a noise sample to the next target image patch, conditioned on the output hidden state. At inference, this allows for generating images by iteratively guiding noise to create the next patch.

color.semantic_mapping: blue transformer blocks, gray token surfaces, dark flow arrows, and image-patch thumbnails

encodings.color: transformer, token surface, and flow roles
encodings.shape: rounded blocks, token boxes, arrows, patch thumbnails, and flow inset
encodings.line: solid sequence arrows and dashed cross-reference arrows
encodings.facet: main pipeline versus patch-wise flow-matching inset
encodings.text: direct component, token, and loss labels

figures.data_and_statistics: Mechanism illustration only. It contains no sample, unit, aggregation, denominator, repeat, uncertainty, or failure count; dog/on/rock and patch thumbnails are explanatory examples.
figures.evidence_relation: Introduction unified multimodal next-token claim -> Figure 1 interface -> §2.1 Eq. (1)-(2) unified objective -> §2.2 tokenizer/causal transformer/157M patch-wise head -> Tables 2-3 main comparisons and Tables 4-5 head ablation.
design_strengths: One page connects token serialization, modality-specific heads, and patch-wise flow matching.
The right inset turns the abstract loss into target/noise/velocity operations.
Arrow direction and direct labels reduce dependence on a separate legend.
design_weaknesses: The main pipeline and inset are dense; token thumbnails and loss labels become small at print size.
Key dimensions such as 16 channels, 256 image tokens, and 157M parameters are absent from the visual.
The image patches are illustrative assets and cannot carry performance evidence.
figures.reusable_pattern: Use a unified sequence backbone plus one local operator inset to explain both system interface and the core training computation.

evidence.label: p. 2 §2.1 / Figure 1 unified token sequence and patch-wise flow-matching inset

figures.label: Figure 3

caption.text: Figure 3: Evolution of per-token mean and variance over sampling steps under two CFG settings. At CFG = 1.5, the mean and variance stay close to 0 and 1, respectively, indicating stability. At CFG = 3.0, they drift significantly, causing image quality degradation. With normalization, the distributions of output latents remain stable across all CFG settings.

Six output thumbnails are qualitative examples.
figures.evidence_relation: §5.2 Eq. (4) CFG interpolation -> Figure 3 mean/variance drift diagnosis -> Eq. (3) and Algorithm 1 token-wise normalization -> Figure 4 noise robustness and Figure A3 latent distributions.

Charts and output thumbnails make a distributional mechanism legible without a second figure.

tables.label: Table 1
tables.uncertainty: No uncertainty: this is a configuration table. K/B/T suffixes, CE:MSE, and ratio denominators are not fully defined in the caption.
tables.data_and_statistics: Training stages list learning rate, scheduler, weight decay, CE:MSE loss weight, steps, warm-up, sequence length, image area, image tokens, and training tokens; the lower group lists four data ratios.
tables.evidence_relation: §3 training recipes -> Table 1 curriculum/configuration dictionary -> Stage 1/2/Annealing/SFT/DPO explanations -> Tables 2-3 results and Table A3 cost boundary.
design_strengths: Two-level phase header makes the curriculum scanable.
Hyperparameters and data mixture share one compact decision surface.
design_weaknesses: Caption does not define abbreviations, suffixes, units, or frozen-tokenizer exceptions.
Many rows and long ranges reduce scan speed; there is no explicit train/freeze column.
tables.reusable_pattern: Use nested phase headers and separate hyperparameter/data-ratio row groups, while putting units and freeze state in the header or caption.

tables.label: Table 2

caption.text: Table 2: Comparison of image-text alignment on GenEval (Ghosh et al., 2023), GenAI-Bench (Lin et al., 2024), and DPG-Bench (Hu et al., 2024). * result is with rewriting. † result is with Self-CoT.

tables.uncertainty: No uncertainty, denominator, seed, or repeat information; point scores and `-` missing values only.
tables.data_and_statistics: Mixed proprietary, diffusion, and autoregressive model rows report GenEval, GenAI-Bench Basic/Advanced, and DPG-Bench; slash/asterisk/dagger protocols alter the input procedure.
tables.evidence_relation: Introduction AR quality claim -> §4.1 -> Table 2 main comparison -> Tables A1/A2 extended OneIG/WISE evidence -> Conclusion SOTA/competitive language.
design_strengths: Model-family groups and arrows make comparison scope explicit.
Ours row color plus bold/underline marks help locate the intended reference.
design_weaknesses: Raw, rewriting, and Self-CoT values are mixed in one table; cross-protocol values are not independent measurements.
No sample, uncertainty, cost, or failure column supports a universal ranking.
tables.reusable_pattern: Use model-family row groups and a highlighted reference row, but split protocol-changing results into separate columns with denominator and evaluation details.

G_SC, G_PQ, and G_O refer to the metrics evaluated by GPT-4.1 (OpenAI, 2025a). Performance is evaluated based on the NextStep-1-Edit with 1:1 aspect ratio.

design_strengths: Nested EN/CN/ImgEdit headers preserve task-language structure.
Caption states judge and 1:1 aspect-ratio condition.
design_weaknesses: Base versus editing-finetuned model naming is inconsistent between prose, caption, and row.
Heterogeneous judges/datasets are placed together without range, sample, or uncertainty context.

tables.label: Table 4

caption.text: Table 4: Configurations for different flow-matching heads.

tables.uncertainty: No uncertainty: layer, hidden-size, and parameter-count metadata.

tables.label: Table 5

caption.text: Table 5: Quantitative results for different flow-matching head configurations. All variants are finetuned from the baseline with a newly initialized head.

tables.uncertainty: No uncertainty: GenEval, GenAI-Bench, and DPG-Bench are single point estimates.

tables.evidence_relation: Table 4 capacities -> Table 5 head-only point estimates -> Figure 2 outputs -> §5.1 claim that the transformer carries core generative logic.
design_strengths: Baseline and variants share columns, enabling direct within-ablation scanning.
Caption states the newly initialized-head control.

tables.label: Table 6

caption.text: Table 6: Comparison of reconstruction performance on ImageNet-1K 256×256 (Deng et al., 2009).

tables.uncertainty: No uncertainty, reconstruction sample count, protocol, or failure count; PSNR and SSIM are point estimates.

design_strengths: Tokenizer-family groups keep discrete/continuous representation differences visible.
Latent shape and two reconstruction metrics share one compact table.
design_weaknesses: Different tokenizer training/decoding protocols are not stated in the caption.
Highlights emphasize relative rank without sample size or uncertainty, so point gaps can be over-read.

tables.label: Table A1

caption.text: Table A1: Comparison on OneIG-Bench (Chang et al., 2025) in English prompts.

tables.uncertainty: No uncertainty, prompt count, scorer, seed, or failure column; all cells are benchmark point scores.
tables.data_and_statistics: Six OneIG-Bench dimensions (Alignment, Text, Reasoning, Style, Diversity, Overall) are given for 24 model rows under three family groups, including NextStep-1.
tables.evidence_relation: §4.1 “full results in section A” -> Table A1 extension -> Table 2 main comparison and Figure A1 qualitative showcase.
design_strengths: Dimension columns expose which aspects drive Overall rather than collapsing to one score.
The same model-family grouping and ours-row highlight as Table 2 aid cross-reference.
design_weaknesses: 27 visible body rows and three-decimal values make the table dense.
Caption omits dimension definitions, sample count, evaluation procedure, and uncertainty despite prose using “significant advantage.”
tables.reusable_pattern: Use an appendix full-result table with the same model grouping as the main result, but add dimension definitions and protocol metadata.

tables.label: Table A2

caption.text: Table A2: Comparison of world knowledge reasoning on WISE (Niu et al., 2025). † result is with Self-CoT.

tables.uncertainty: No uncertainty or sample denominator; slash cells combine raw and Self-CoT/rewrite point scores, and `-` denotes absent protocol.
tables.data_and_statistics: Six WISE domain scores, Overall, and Overall (Rewrite) are reported across proprietary, diffusion, and autoregressive groups; BAGEL and NextStep-1 contain raw/rewrite pairs.
tables.evidence_relation: Knowledge-aware generation claim -> Table A2 raw/rewrite WISE extension -> Table 2/A1 AR comparison -> conclusion semantic-alignment claim.
design_strengths: Domain columns make the claimed world-knowledge coverage inspectable.
Raw/rewrite values and family rows preserve protocol and comparison context better than one aggregate.
design_weaknesses: Slash values make two protocols look like one measurement and are incomplete across models.
Caption does not explain rewrite/Self-CoT transformation, pairing, or uncertainty.
tables.reusable_pattern: Give raw and rewrite/Self-CoT separate blocks or columns, with paired sample counts and protocol definitions.

tables.label: Table A3

caption.text: Table A3: Inference latency breakdown at 983 TFLOP/s compute and 3.36 TB/s memory bandwidth.

tables.uncertainty: No measurement uncertainty: the table is a theoretical batch-1 breakdown under stated H100 compute and bandwidth assumptions.
tables.data_and_statistics: Sequence lengths 256/1024/4096 report last-token latency for LLM Decoder, LM Head, and FM Head in ms, plus accumulated Total and w/o FM Head in s.
tables.evidence_relation: Appendix D sequential-decoding limitation -> Table A3 component/accumulated latency -> serial LLM/FM bottleneck explanation -> proposed distillation/speculative/multi-token acceleration.
design_strengths: Nested headers separate last-token and accumulated units.
The `w/o FM Head` counterfactual exposes component contribution directly.
design_weaknesses: Theoretical FLOP/bandwidth values are not wall-clock profiling and lack batch/parallelism/memory assumptions.
Batch size 1 and estimation status are in surrounding prose rather than the caption.
tables.reusable_pattern: Separate theoretical from measured cost and put hardware, batch, parallelism, and repeat assumptions in the table caption.

cross_object_system.visual_narrative: Figure 1 defines the continuous-token causal interface; Table 1 fixes training recipe; Tables 2-3 report T2I/editing comparisons; Figure 2 and Tables 4-5 test flow-matching-head capacity; Figure 3, Figure 4, and Table 6 connect CFG/noise/latent dispersion to reconstruction. Appendix Figures A1-A5, Tables A1-A3 extend capabilities, data/tokenizer diagnostics, failures, fixes, and latency.
cross_object_system.caption_system: Captions use label plus noun-phrase title and optional setup sentence, usually without bold headline, sample/seed, or uncertainty template. Figure 3 is the only caption that states a principal stability/drift finding; most conclusions remain in surrounding prose.
cross_object_system.table_header_system: Main and appendix result tables use model-family row groups, metric-direction arrows, nested benchmark headers, and a light-blue ours row; bold/underline mark best/second-best values. Configuration tables use phase/tokenizer groups but do not consistently encode units, protocol, or cost.
cross_object_system.method_result_ablation_link: Figure 1 -> Tables 2-3 supplies interface-to-result linkage; Tables 4-5 plus Figure 2 supply head-size ablation; Figure 3 plus Algorithm 1 supply normalization mechanism; Figure 4, Figure A3, and Table 6 supply noise/dispersion/reconstruction diagnostics. Links are cited in prose, but controls, seeds, and uncertainty are generally absent.
cross_object_system.main_appendix_link: 正文 directs readers to Appendix A for qualitative and benchmark extensions, B for data pipelines, C for tokenizer code, and D for artifacts/latency. The appendix adds useful qualitative and implementation context but does not add failure rates, measured profiling, full data provenance, or editable visual sources.
cross_object_system.typography_consistency: NimbusRomNo9L and Computer Modern dominate article text, captions, tables, and equations. Raster diagrams introduce sans-serif/Calibri/Times substyles and much smaller labels, making embedded figure text the main cross-object readability risk.
cross_object_system.color_consistency: Blue consistently signals architecture, ours rows, or newer-version headers; purple/orange/green/blue identify curves and corresponding photo borders. Figure A2 adds orange-red/green process semantics. No global palette or shape redundancy is documented, so Figure 3/4 curves and blue table rows are not fully grayscale-safe.

most_reusable_patterns: Figure 1 main flow plus local loss inset for interface and operator explanation.
Figure 3/4 aligned mechanism curves with condition-matched qualitative strips.
Table 2/3 model-family groups, direction arrows, nested headers, and ours-row highlighting.
Figure A2 global pipeline plus detailed panels, and Figure A4 failure-mode rows.
failure_patterns: Large qualitative montages lack prompt, seed, selection, and coverage metadata.
Curves and tables almost universally omit denominator, repeats, or uncertainty.
Raw/rewrite/Self-CoT protocols and base/edit variants are mixed in comparison surfaces.
Appendix shows failures and theoretical latency but no incidence rates, measured profiling, or editable figure/table source.
final_judgment.one_sentence_visual_strategy: The paper builds a cold-blue causal-architecture spine and joins tokenizer mechanism curves, cross-model point tables, and dense qualitative outputs into an interface-to-quality-to-stability narrative, while relying heavily on color and selected examples and leaving statistical and reproducibility metadata thin.
